angle: Explain Every Door Direct Mail (EDDM) in plain terms for a local business owner who has never heard of it -- what it is, how it differs from a purchased mailing list, and why the Postal Service runs it.
Make the case that the carrier route itself is a better 'list' than any mailing list a small business could buy -- no stale contacts, no purchase, every real address included.
Compare what it really costs to reach a home by mail versus a boosted social post or local digital ad, in terms of durability and how long the impression sticks around a household.
Explain why claiming your category on a route early matters more than chasing the single biggest route, since exclusivity -- not size -- is what protects a spot from a competitor.
Help a first-time advertiser set realistic expectations for what a mailer can and can't do on its first run, without promising a specific number.
Cover the most common design mistakes that make an otherwise fine mailer get ignored -- too much text, no clear offer, no obvious next step.
Explain why a single mailer rarely converts on its own and how repeat mailings on the same route compound over a few cycles.
Explain why households that just moved in are unusually receptive to print mail right when they're deciding who to call for local services.
Discuss timing a mailer to the season -- matching when a mailer lands to when that category's customers are actually making decisions.
Make the case for pairing a physical mailer with a strong Google Business Profile, so someone who saw the postcard can find and trust the business online afterward.
Give simple, low-tech ways a small business can track whether a mailer actually worked -- a dedicated phone extension, a mention-this-card offer, asking new customers how they heard.
Explain why reaching renters matters just as much as homeowners for most local service categories, and how a purchased homeowner list quietly leaves them out.
Discuss what kind of offer actually gets a postcard picked up off the kitchen counter instead of going straight to the recycling bin.
Make the case that printed mail still carries a trust signal a paid social ad doesn't, especially for a newer business without reviews yet.
Help a business owner think through which carrier route is actually 'near' them in a practical sense, not just the closest one on a map.
Sketch a simple, low-budget local marketing mix built around one mailer plus a couple of free or cheap channels, for a business with no marketing budget to speak of.
Compare EDDM mailers to door hangers, flyers, and other cheap local ad formats -- what each is actually good for.
Write a short, practical checklist for a business owner who has never advertised offline before and is nervous about getting it wrong.
Explain how a physical mailer can kick-start word of mouth in a tight-knit town, where people talk about what showed up in their mailbox.
Explain which kinds of categories tend to fill up fastest on a route and why, without naming specific competitors or making claims about ZipCarrd's own fill rates.
Make the case that the real return on a flat-rate mailer should be measured against a customer's lifetime value, not just the first call it generates.
Help a business with no real marketing budget think through what a sensible, small first step into advertising looks like.
